templates.name: 5-Day Paris Packing List
templates.description: Everything for a 5-day Paris city break — documents, layers, walking shoes, and anti-theft essentials.
items: Passport, plus a printed and offline photo of your ID
Visa or ETIAS authorization, if your nationality needs one
Two cards and about €50 in cash
Phone and a charger with an EU plug adapter
Universal travel adapter
Comfortable, broken-in walking shoes
Five layerable tops and two bottoms
A light jacket or trench
Compact umbrella
Crossbody anti-theft bag with a zip
Reusable water bottle
Pre-booked Louvre and Eiffel Tower tickets, or a Paris Museum Pass
Metro (RATP) app and an offline map
A translation app and a few basic French phrases
Daily medications and a small first-aid kit
Sunglasses
Portable power bank
Toiletries in a clear bag, packed for 3 days

templates.name: Weekend Trip Packing List
templates.description: A carry-on-friendly list for a 2-3 day getaway — outfits, toiletries, tech, and easy-to-forget extras.
items: ID or passport and your booking confirmations
Phone charger and a power bank
Two-to-three days of clothes in one color family
One "nice" outfit for dinner out
Pajamas, plus fresh socks and underwear per day and one spare
A light layer — sweater or jacket — for evenings
Comfortable walking shoes, plus one dressier pair
Toiletries in travel-size bottles under 100ml
Toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, and skincare
Daily medications, painkillers, and plasters
Sunglasses and, if sunny, sunscreen
Reusable water bottle
Chargers and cables for every device
A book, headphones, or downloaded shows for the journey
A small day bag or tote for outings
House keys and a card for parking or transit
A foldable tote or laundry bag for dirty clothes

templates.name: International Flight Checklist
templates.description: Pre-flight documents, carry-on rules, and airport timing so nothing derails an international departure.
items: Passport valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates
Visa, ETA, or ETIAS for your destination
Printed or offline boarding pass and hotel confirmation
Travel insurance details and an emergency contact card
Copies of your passport, stored separately and in the cloud
Local currency plus a card that works abroad
Universal power adapter for your destination's plug type
Power bank in your carry-on
Medications in your carry-on, in original packaging
Liquids under 100ml in a clear resealable bag for cabin security
Noise-cancelling headphones or earbuds, with content downloaded
Neck pillow, eye mask, and earplugs for long-haul
Refillable water bottle — empty through security, fill after
Snacks that clear customs
A change of clothes and essentials in your carry-on
Check your baggage allowance and weigh your bag at home
Offline maps and a translation app downloaded before you fly
A roaming plan or local eSIM set up before departure
Arrive at the airport about 3 hours before an international departure

templates.name: Beach Vacation Packing List
templates.description: Swimwear, reef-safe sunscreen, sun protection, and the beach-day extras people always forget.
items: Passport or ID and travel documents
Two or three swimsuits
Reef-safe sunscreen SPF 30+ and after-sun
Wide-brim hat and UV-protection sunglasses
Lightweight cover-up or kaftan
Flip-flops plus one pair of walking sandals
Quick-dry beach towel
Breathable, light clothing for hot days
One warm layer for air-conditioned restaurants and evenings
Aloe vera or after-sun for sunburn
Insect repellent
Waterproof phone pouch and a dry bag for valuables
Refillable water bottle
Beach bag or tote
Daily medications plus motion-sickness tablets for boat trips
Basic first-aid: plasters, antiseptic, painkillers
Portable fan or cooling towel for extreme heat
Snorkel gear if you have it
E-reader or book with a waterproof case
Power bank and travel adapter

templates.name: Business Trip Checklist
templates.description: Laptop and adapters, wrinkle-free outfits, presentation tech, and the work-travel essentials.
items: Photo ID or passport and any visa needed
Boarding passes, hotel, and rental-car confirmations
Laptop, charger, and a spare charging cable
Phone, power bank, and adapter for your destination
Business cards
Notebook and pens, or a tablet and stylus
Two or three wrinkle-resistant business outfits
One smart-casual outfit for dinners or downtime
Comfortable dress shoes you've already worn in
Toiletries and a grooming kit in travel sizes
Presentation dongles and an HDMI or USB-C adapter
Printed copies of key documents as a backup
Daily medications and basic painkillers
Reusable water bottle and a few snacks
Noise-cancelling headphones for the flight and the hotel
Expense receipts folder or app set up before you go
A small multi-port charger
A light layer for cold conference rooms and planes

templates.name: Vacation Preparation Checklist
templates.description: Everything to sort before you go — documents, insurance, money, home, and pet care.
items: Book flights and accommodation, and save the confirmations offline
Check your passport is valid for at least six months past your return date
Apply for any visa or travel authorization (ESTA, eTA) well ahead
Check recommended or required vaccinations for your destination
Buy travel insurance that covers medical care and trip cancellation
Notify your bank and card issuer of your travel dates
Get some local currency and a card with no foreign-transaction fees
Arrange airport transfer or parking for both ends of the trip
Arrange pet care, house-sitting, or plant watering
Pause mail, deliveries, and any subscriptions you won't use
Set an out-of-office reply and hand off anything urgent at work
Check the weather, local holidays, and dress code at your destination
Download offline maps, a translation app, and your airline and booking apps
Photograph your passport, tickets, and insurance, and store copies in the cloud
Sort your phone plan: international roaming or a local or eSIM data plan
Leave your itinerary and copies of key documents with someone at home

templates.name: Road Trip Checklist
templates.description: Car checks, route and maps, emergency kit, snacks, and comfort for the long drive.
items: Check tire pressure and tread, including the spare
Top up oil, coolant, and washer fluid, and test the brakes and lights
Confirm your license, registration, and insurance are current and in the car
Plan the route with fuel and rest stops, and download offline maps
Check your roadside assistance coverage and save the number
Pack an emergency kit: jumper cables, tire inflator, flashlight, and a warning triangle
Pack a first aid kit and any daily medications
Keep water and snacks within the driver's reach
Charge every device and bring a car charger and a long cable
Download a playlist, podcasts, or audiobooks for offline listening
Bring cash and coins for tolls, parking, and small vendors
Set up a phone mount so navigation stays in view, hands-free
Pack sunglasses, and pillows and blankets for passengers
Bring wet wipes, hand sanitizer, paper towels, and a trash bag
Share your route and expected arrival time with someone
Keep a paper map or written directions as a backup

templates.name: Camping Trip Checklist
templates.description: Tent and sleeping gear, cooking, water, layers, safety, and Leave No Trace basics.
items: Reserve your campsite and check its rules on fires, pets, and check-in
Pack the tent, groundsheet, and enough stakes, and pitch it once at home
Bring sleeping bags rated for the night-time low, plus sleeping pads
Pack a camp stove with enough fuel, a lighter, and waterproof matches
Bring cookware, utensils, a sharp knife, and biodegradable soap
Plan your meals and store food in a sealed cooler or bear-proof container
Bring plenty of drinking water, plus a filter or purification tablets
Pack headlamps, a lantern, and spare batteries
Dress in layers, with rain gear and a warm hat for the evening
Bring sturdy, broken-in footwear and several pairs of dry socks
Pack a first aid kit, insect repellent, and sunscreen
Carry a paper map and compass or GPS, and tell someone your plans
Bring trash bags and pack out everything you bring in
Pack a multi-tool, duct tape, and paracord for quick repairs
Check the forecast and pack for the worst weather it suggests
Bring toilet paper, a trowel, and hand sanitizer

templates.name: Moving House Checklist
templates.description: A step-by-step 8-week timeline — quotes, decluttering, utilities, and moving day, in order.
items: Eight weeks out: set your moving date and budget, and decide between movers and a DIY van
Seven weeks out: declutter room by room and sell, donate, or bin what you won't take
Six weeks out: book your movers or hire van, and reserve any elevator or parking permits
Five weeks out: gather boxes, tape, bubble wrap, and markers, and start packing rarely-used rooms
Four weeks out: notify your landlord or list your home, and confirm your new address details
Three weeks out: transfer or set up utilities, internet, and insurance at the new place
Two weeks out: file your change of address and redirect your mail
One week out: pack everything but essentials, label boxes by room, and defrost the freezer
Two days out: pack an essentials box (chargers, toiletries, meds, a change of clothes) and keep it with you
Moving day: photograph meter readings, do a final walkthrough, and check every room and cupboard before you leave
First day in: find the fuse box, stopcock, and thermostat, and test that the utilities work
First week in: unpack essentials, update your address on IDs and accounts, and register with a local doctor

templates.name: First Apartment Essentials Checklist
templates.description: Bedding, a starter kitchen, cleaning and tools, plus the renter admin for your first place.
items: Bed, mattress, pillows, and two sets of sheets
Bath towels, hand towels, and a shower curtain
A basic kitchen kit: pots, a pan, a chef's knife, a cutting board, and a can opener
Plates, bowls, glasses, mugs, and cutlery for four
Cooking basics: spatula, wooden spoon, measuring cups, a mixing bowl, a colander
Food storage containers, foil, cling film, and bin bags
A microwave, kettle, or toaster if not already provided
Cleaning kit: all-purpose spray, dish soap, sponges, a mop, broom, and vacuum
Laundry basket, detergent, and a drying rack
Toilet paper, hand soap, and a plunger
A basic toolkit: hammer, screwdrivers, tape measure, and picture hooks
Extension leads and enough phone and laptop chargers
A first-aid kit and basic medicines
Working smoke and carbon-monoxide detectors
Trash and recycling bins
Light bulbs and a lamp or nightlight for each room
Renter's insurance and copies of your lease and inventory
A shower caddy, bath mat, and toothbrush holder
Pantry staples: salt, oil, pasta, coffee or tea
A doormat and a few command hooks for keys

templates.name: Change of Address Checklist
templates.description: Who to tell when you move, in the right order — mail, government, banks, utilities, and more.
items: Redirect your mail with your postal service
File your official change of address with the government: voter roll, tax authority, and driver's license agency
Update your bank, credit cards, and any loan or mortgage providers
Tell your employer's payroll and HR, and update pension or retirement accounts
Update your insurance: home or renter's, car, health, and life policies
Switch or transfer utilities: electricity, gas, water, internet, and phone
Update your doctor, dentist, and pharmacy, and transfer prescriptions
Change your address on subscriptions and deliveries
Update your driving license and vehicle registration
Tell schools or childcare and transfer any records
Update online shopping accounts and digital wallets
Let friends and family know, and update your address on any wills or legal documents

templates.name: New Home Setup Checklist
templates.description: First-days-in tasks — shut-offs, alarms, meter readings, locks, and a deep clean before you unpack.
items: Locate and label the fuse box, water stopcock, and gas shut-off
Test smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms and replace any dead batteries
Take meter readings (gas, electric, water) and send them to your providers
Confirm utilities, heating, and hot water all work
Change the locks, or at least have the keys re-keyed
Set up and test your internet and Wi-Fi
Do a deep clean before furniture arrives
Check for leaks, damp, or pest signs and photograph any issues for your records
Find the nearest hospital, pharmacy, and grocery store
Learn your bin and recycling collection days and where the bins go
Unpack your essentials box first: bedding, toiletries, chargers, and a kettle
Register with a local doctor and dentist
Introduce yourself to the neighbours and ask about parking and building quirks
Update your address on IDs, accounts, and deliveries
Set up a basic first-aid kit and a fire extinguisher
Note your landlord's or property manager's emergency contact
Program the thermostat and check every window and door lock
Plan your furniture layout before hauling heavy items around

templates.name: Packing to Move Checklist
templates.description: Supplies, a room-by-room method, labelling, and the first-night box that saves your first evening.
items: Gather supplies: sturdy boxes in a few sizes, packing tape, bubble wrap, packing paper, and markers
Declutter first — donate, sell, or bin anything you won't use
Pack room by room, finishing one before you start the next
Label every box with its room and contents, and mark fragile boxes clearly
Keep boxes under about 15kg
Wrap breakables individually and fill gaps so nothing shifts
Use towels, blankets, and clothing as padding to save on bubble wrap
Keep screws and small parts in labelled bags taped to the furniture they belong to
Photograph the back of your TV and electronics before unplugging them
Pack a "first night" essentials box and keep it with you
Pack a separate valuables bag: documents, jewellery, medications, and small electronics you carry yourself
Empty, clean, and dry appliances, and defrost the freezer at least a day ahead
Seal liquids in bags and pack them upright to stop leaks
Keep a "packing kit" of tape, scissors, and a marker you can always find
Leave clothes on hangers and slip a bin bag over them as a quick wardrobe box
Either empty drawers or wrap the whole unit closed — don't overpack them
Count and number your boxes so you know if any go missing
Load the truck with the heaviest items first and against the cab

templates.name: Newborn First Month Checklist
templates.description: The genuine first-month must-haves — safe sleep, feeding, diapering, and health, no over-buying.
items: 6-8 newborn and 0-3 month bodysuits and sleepers
A safe sleep space (crib, bassinet, or Moses basket) with a firm, flat mattress
4-6 fitted sheets for the mattress
Swaddles or sleep sacks
Newborn diapers and plenty of wipes
Diaper cream and a changing pad
If breastfeeding: nursing bras, breast pads, nipple cream, and a pump if you'll express
If formula feeding: bottles, newborn-flow teats, formula, and a bottle brush
Burp cloths and bibs
A car seat, correctly installed and rear-facing
A soft carrier or sling, and a stroller or pram
Baby bath support, hooded towels, and fragrance-free baby wash
Soft washcloths and a soft-bristle baby brush
A digital thermometer and infant paracetamol
Baby nail clippers or a file
A stack of muslin cloths for everything
Blackout blinds or a dim night light for night feeds
Contact details for your pediatrician and the out-of-hours line
Warm layers, a hat, and mittens if the weather's cold
Postpartum supplies for you: pads, comfortable clothing, and easy snacks

templates.name: Hospital Bag Checklist
templates.description: Packed in three parts — for you, for baby, and for your partner — with the easy-to-forget extras.
items: Photo ID, insurance details, and your hospital notes or birth plan
A comfortable, loose nightgown or two
A warm robe, non-slip socks, and slippers for the ward
Several pairs of high-waisted, disposable, or old underwear
Maternity or heavy-flow pads for after the birth
A nursing bra and breast pads if you plan to breastfeed
Toiletries: toothbrush, toothpaste, lip balm, hair ties, and travel-size wash
A going-home outfit for you
Phone, a long charging cable, and a power bank
Snacks and drinks for a long labour, plus a card for vending machines
For baby: 2-3 bodysuits and sleepers in newborn and 0-3 sizes
For baby: a hat, scratch mittens, and socks
For baby: a swaddle or blanket and a going-home outfit for the season
Newborn diapers and a small pack of wipes
An installed, rear-facing car seat for the drive home
For your partner: a change of clothes, snacks, toiletries, and their own phone charger
Any regular medications you take, in their original packaging
A pillow from home

templates.name: Baby Registry Checklist
templates.description: The essentials to register — car seat and stroller, sleep, clothing sizes, feeding, and a cash fund.
items: Car seat (infant or convertible), rear-facing and correctly rated
Stroller or travel system that fits your car seat
Crib or bassinet with a firm, flat mattress and 2-4 fitted sheets
Swaddles and sleep sacks
6-8 bodysuits and sleepers each in 0-3 and 3-6 months
Diapers in a range of sizes and plenty of wipes
Changing pad and a diaper caddy or diaper bag
Feeding gear: bottles and teats, plus a breast pump or nursing pillow if breastfeeding
Burp cloths, bibs, and muslins
Baby bath, hooded towels, and fragrance-free wash
A carrier or sling for hands-free days
A baby monitor
High chair (for later, but useful to register now)
Thermometer, nail clippers, and a basic grooming kit
A few developmental toys, board books, and a play mat
Blackout blinds or a night light
A comfortable feeding chair, or a spot set up for feeds
Gift cards or a "cash fund" for big-ticket items and post-birth needs

templates.name: Diaper Bag Checklist
templates.description: Diapers and wipes, spare outfits, feeding, and a first-aid kit — plus what to pack for yourself.
items: 4-6 diapers, more for a long day out
A travel pack of wipes
A portable, foldable changing mat
Diaper cream in a small tube
Scented bags for dirty diapers
1-2 full changes of clothes for baby
Muslins or burp cloths
Feeding supplies: a bottle and formula, or a nursing cover if you prefer one
A bib and a few napkins
A pacifier or two, in a clean case
Hand sanitizer and a few tissues
A small first-aid kit: a thermometer, plasters, and infant paracetamol
Sun hat and baby-safe sunscreen in summer, or an extra layer and hat in winter
A light blanket or swaddle
A small toy or two to distract a fussy baby
A snack and water for you
A spare shirt for you
Restock it after every outing so it's always ready to grab

templates.name: Baby-Proofing Checklist
templates.description: Room-by-room home safety — anchor furniture, secure chemicals and cords, gates, and battery safety.
items: Anchor bookcases, dressers, and the TV to the wall
Cover unused electrical outlets with safety plugs
Install safety gates at the top and bottom of stairs
Add cabinet and drawer latches, especially where cleaning products or knives live
Move all medicines, cleaning products, and chemicals up high and locked away
Fit stove knob covers and turn pot handles toward the back
Secure blind and curtain cords out of reach
Pad sharp furniture corners and edges
Set your water heater to 49°C / 120°F to prevent scalds
Keep small objects, button batteries, and magnets off the floor and out of reach
Use door-knob covers or locks on rooms that are off-limits
Check that smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms work, on every level
Keep the crib clear of pillows, bumpers, and toys, and away from windows and cords
Latch the toilet lid and keep the bathroom door closed
Tuck away or cover trailing electrical cords
Move toxic houseplants out of reach, or remove them
Crawl each room at your baby's eye level to spot hazards you'd miss standing up
Save poison-control and emergency numbers where everyone can find them

templates.name: Wedding Planning Checklist
templates.description: A month-by-month 12-month timeline — budget, venue, vendors, invites, and the final week, in order.
items: 12+ months out: set your total budget, rough guest count, and your top 3 priorities as a couple
11 months out: tour and book your venue and lock in the date
10 months out: book the photographer and videographer, and hire a planner if you want one
9 months out: book the caterer and start dress and suit shopping
8 months out: book the band or DJ, the officiant, and the florist
7 months out: order your dress, book hotel room blocks for guests, and plan the honeymoon
6 months out: send save-the-dates and start building your gift registry
5 months out: order invitations, plan the ceremony, and choose your wedding party's attire
4 months out: do a cake tasting and order the cake, and buy the wedding rings
3 months out: finalize the menu, book hair and makeup, and apply for the marriage license
2 months out: mail the invitations with a clear RSVP date, and do a hair and makeup trial
6 weeks out: final dress fitting, and start the seating chart
1 month out: confirm the final headcount with all vendors, make final payments, and write your vows
2 weeks out: finalize the seating chart, break in your shoes, and confirm the day-of timeline with every vendor
1 week out: pack for the honeymoon, assemble welcome bags, and delegate day-of tasks to trusted people
Day before: attend the rehearsal and rehearsal dinner, drop off items at the venue, and get an early night

templates.name: Wedding Day Timeline
templates.description: An hour-by-hour sample schedule from getting ready to the send-off, built around a 4pm ceremony.
items: 8:00 am — Light breakfast, hydrate, and shower
9:00 am — Hair and makeup begins for the wedding party
11:00 am — Photographer arrives for detail shots: rings, dress, invitations, shoes
12:00 pm — Getting-ready photos; the wedding party gets dressed
12:30 pm — Light lunch and drinks for everyone getting ready
1:00 pm — Get into the dress or suit with help on hand for buttons and ties
1:30 pm — First look and private couple portraits
2:00 pm — Wedding-party and immediate-family group photos
3:00 pm — Tuck away to freshen up as early guests start arriving
3:30 pm — Pre-ceremony music starts and ushers seat guests
4:00 pm — Ceremony begins
4:30 pm — Ceremony ends; cocktail hour starts and any remaining family photos are taken
5:30 pm — Guests move to the reception; the couple is announced in
5:45 pm — First dance
6:00 pm — Dinner is served, opening with a short welcome toast
7:00 pm — Speeches and toasts
7:45 pm — Cake cutting
8:00 pm — Dance floor opens with the parent dances
10:30 pm — Last dance and grand send-off
11:00 pm — Vendors break down; assign someone to collect gifts, cards, and decor

templates.name: Birthday Party Checklist
templates.description: Everything for a birthday party — invites, cake, food, decor, games, and the day-of setup.
items: Set the date, start and end time, and a rough guest count
Set a budget and split it across food, cake, decor, and entertainment
Pick a theme or color scheme
Choose and book the venue, or prep your home
Send invitations 3 to 4 weeks ahead with an RSVP date
Plan the menu: food, drinks, and any dietary or allergy needs
Order or bake the cake, and buy candles and a lighter
Plan decorations: balloons, banner, tablecloth, and centerpieces
Plan activities and entertainment: games, a playlist, or a photo backdrop
Buy party favors or goodie bags
Buy or wrap the birthday gift
Stock disposables: plates, cups, napkins, utensils, and trash bags
Prep a music playlist and test the speaker
Charge your phone or camera for photos
Day-of: set up 1 to 2 hours early, chill the drinks, and set out food just before guests arrive
Assign someone to greet guests and someone to manage the cake and candles moment

templates.name: Event Planning Checklist
templates.description: A full planning list for any event — goals, budget, venue, catering, AV, run-of-show, and teardown.
items: Define the event's goal and how you'll measure success
Set the date and hold a backup date
Set the budget and set up a simple way to track spending against it
Estimate the headcount and build the guest or attendee list
Book the venue and confirm its capacity and layout
Confirm exactly what the venue includes: tables, chairs, AV, wifi, parking
Hire the caterer and confirm dietary and allergy options
Arrange AV: sound, microphones, projector, and screens
Book speakers, entertainment, or a host, and confirm their needs
Build the run-of-show: a minute-by-minute timeline for the day
Send invitations or open registration, and track RSVPs
Plan decor, signage, and any branding or printed materials
Sort transportation, directions, and parking for attendees
Confirm permits, licenses, and event insurance
Line up staff or volunteers and give each a clear role
Prepare a day-of contact sheet with every vendor and lead's number
Plan cleanup, teardown, and who returns rentals
After the event: send thank-yous and gather feedback while it's fresh

templates.name: Party Planning Checklist
templates.description: A simple plan for any get-together — guest list, food and drinks, decor, playlist, and setup.
items: Pick the occasion, date, and start and end time
Set a headcount and a budget
Choose a venue or prep your own space
Send invites 2 to 3 weeks ahead with an RSVP request
Plan the menu and quantities, allowing for dietary needs
Plan drinks: alcoholic and non-alcoholic, plus plenty of ice
Write a shopping list and shop 1 to 2 days ahead
Plan decor and lighting for the mood you want
Build a playlist long enough to cover the whole night, and test the speaker
Plan one activity or icebreaker if guests won't all know each other
Arrange seating and flow so people naturally mingle
Stock essentials: cups, plates, napkins, serving utensils, and trash bags
Clear space and set up a spot for coats and bags
Day-of: cook and prep early, chill the drinks, and give the bathroom a quick tidy
Ask a friend to co-host: manage the door and keep drinks and food topped up
Set out food about 15 minutes before guests are due

templates.name: Holiday Season Prep Checklist
templates.description: Get ahead of the holidays — budget, gifts, decorating, meals, cards, travel, and year-end tasks.
items: Set an overall holiday budget covering gifts, food, travel, and decor
Make a gift list with a set amount per person
Start shopping early and spread purchases across several weeks
Note shipping deadlines for anything ordered online or posted abroad
Plan holiday meals and menus, including any guest dietary needs
Order or reserve anything special ahead of time — a turkey, a cake, or catering
Write a grocery list and buy non-perishables early
Send holiday cards or digital greetings, checking your address list first
Decorate the home, and test lights before hanging them
Plan and RSVP to gatherings, and confirm who's hosting what
Book travel and accommodation, and arrange pet or house sitting if you're away
Buy wrapping paper, tape, gift bags, tags, and ribbon in one trip
Wrap and label gifts as you get them, rather than all at once
Prepare for guests: spare bedding, towels, and a few easy extra meals
Plan a New Year's celebration or a quiet night in
Wrap up year-end tasks: donations, appointments, and next year's calendar

templates.name: Morning Routine Checklist
templates.description: A step-by-step routine to start the day right — light, water, movement, and a clear plan.
items: Wake at a consistent time and get up without hitting snooze
Get bright light within 30 to 60 minutes: open the curtains or step outside
Drink a large glass of water
Make your bed
Move your body for 5 to 10 minutes: stretch, walk, or a light workout
Brush your teeth and wash your face, or splash with cold water to wake up
Do 5 minutes of breathing, meditation, or quiet before the noise starts
Write your top 3 priorities for the day
Eat a protein-forward breakfast
Take any vitamins or supplements
Delay caffeine until about 90 minutes after waking
Shower and get dressed
Review your calendar and to-do list for the day
Keep your phone and email out of the first 30 to 60 minutes

templates.name: Meal Prep Checklist
templates.description: Plan, shop, batch-cook, and portion — everything to prep a week of meals in one session.
items: Pick 2 to 3 recipes that reheat well
Plan the week's meals: breakfasts, lunches, dinners, and snacks
Check what you already have in the fridge, freezer, and pantry
Write a shopping list grouped by store section
Do a single grocery run for the whole week
Wash and chop all your vegetables at once
Cook grains and starches in bulk: rice, quinoa, pasta, or potatoes
Batch-cook proteins: chicken, ground meat, beans, tofu, or hard-boiled eggs
Roast a big tray of mixed vegetables
Make one sauce or dressing to vary the flavor across meals
Portion meals into containers and label each with the date
Cool food fully before sealing the lids
Freeze any portions you won't eat within 3 to 4 days
Prep grab-and-go snacks: cut fruit, portioned nuts, or yogurt cups
Arrange the fridge by day or meal so the right container is easy to grab
Clean as you go and wash your containers so next week is easy

templates.name: Gym Bag Checklist
templates.description: Everything for a gym session — workout gear, shower kit, and the easy-to-forget extras.
items: Workout clothes: a moisture-wicking top and shorts or leggings
Proper training shoes for your workout
A spare pair of socks
Water bottle
Small sweat towel for wiping down equipment and yourself
Padlock for the locker
Headphones, charged
Lifting gloves or wrist straps, if you lift heavy
A resistance band for warm-ups and activation
A pre- or post-workout snack or protein shake
Deodorant
Shower kit: travel soap or body wash, shampoo, and flip-flops
A quick-dry towel for showering
A full change of clean clothes and underwear
A dry bag or plastic bag for sweaty clothes
Membership card or the gym app on your phone
Hair ties or a headband
Phone plus a charger or power bank

templates.name: Self-Care Checklist
templates.description: A menu for mind and body — sleep, movement, connection, and real rest to actually recharge.
items: Drink enough water through the day
Get 7 to 9 hours of sleep
Move your body for 20 to 30 minutes, even just a walk
Eat at least one balanced, home-cooked meal
Step outside for fresh air and daylight
Take a real break from screens
Do one thing purely because you enjoy it
Connect with a friend or someone you love
Write down 3 things you're grateful for
Tidy one small space to clear your head
Say no to one thing that drains you
Do a 5-minute breathing or meditation session
Stretch or take a warm bath to release tension
Set a limit on doomscrolling and social media
Take any medications or supplements you need
Plan something small to look forward to
Check in with yourself: how am I actually feeling today?

templates.name: Marathon Training Checklist
templates.description: From first run to finish line — shoes, a plan, long runs, tapering, and race day, in order.
items: Get a medical check-up before you start, especially if you're new to running or have any health concerns
Buy properly fitted running shoes, ideally after a gait analysis at a running store
Choose a 16 to 20 week training plan that matches your current fitness
Set a realistic goal: to finish, or a specific target time
Base phase (weeks 1 to 4): build easy, conversational mileage running 3 to 4 times a week
Add one weekly long run and increase its distance gradually
Include one speed or tempo session each week to build pace
Strength-train twice a week, focusing on core, glutes, and legs
Cross-train on off days with cycling or swimming to build fitness without pounding
Dial in your race-day nutrition and practice fueling on long runs
Prioritize hydration, sleep, and recovery throughout the block
Peak weeks: reach your longest run of about 20 miles (32 km) around 3 weeks out
Taper: cut your mileage over the final 2 to 3 weeks so you arrive fresh
Lay out your race-day gear the night before, using nothing new
Carb-load and hydrate well over the final few days
Race day: start slower than feels easy and stick to your pace and fueling plan
After the race: keep moving to cool down, refuel, hydrate, and rest before running again

templates.name: Gym Workout Checklist
templates.description: A full gym session in order — warm up, upper body, lower body, core, then cool down and log your sets.
items: Set today's focus — full body, or a specific split like push, pull, or legs
Warm up for 5 to 10 minutes with light cardio to raise your heart rate
Do dynamic mobility drills for the joints you're about to train
Start with the biggest compound lifts while you're fresh — squats, deadlifts, bench, or rows
Work your upper body with a push and a pull movement
Work your lower body with a squat or hinge and a single-leg movement
Finish the main work with focused core exercises
Use a weight you can control with good form for every rep
Rest 60 to 120 seconds between heavy sets, less for lighter accessory work
Track each exercise, weight, and reps as you go
Sip water throughout the session, not just at the end
Wipe down each machine and bench, and rerack your weights
Cool down with 5 minutes of easy movement to bring your heart rate down
Stretch the muscles you trained while they're still warm
Log the session and note how it felt for next time

templates.name: Running Prep Checklist
templates.description: Everything before you head out — weather, gear, warm-up, hydration, and your route.
items: Check the forecast and temperature right before you go
Dress in moisture-wicking layers you can shed, not cotton
Lace up proper running shoes with tread and life left in them
Have water ready, and drink if it's hot or you're going long
Plan your route and distance, noting where you can refill or cut it short
Queue a playlist or podcast, but keep one ear on traffic
Tell someone your route, or share your live location if running alone
Do a dynamic warm-up: leg swings, lunges, and high knees
Start with 3 to 5 minutes of brisk walking or an easy jog
Ease into your target pace rather than sprinting off the line
Keep your breathing steady and your shoulders and hands relaxed
Cool down with a few minutes of easy walking at the end
Do your static stretches while your muscles are still warm
Log your distance, time, and how you felt

templates.name: Yoga Session Checklist
templates.description: A calming home flow — set up, breathe, warm up, move through poses, and rest in savasana.
items: Set up a quiet space and lay out a non-slip mat
Keep props within reach: a block, a strap, and a cushion or folded blanket
Wear comfortable, stretchy clothing and practice barefoot
Practice on a fairly empty stomach
Silence your phone or set a gentle timer for savasana
Begin seated with a few minutes of slow, deep breathing to center yourself
Warm up with gentle movement: cat-cow, neck rolls, and a few sun salutations
Move through standing poses like warrior and triangle to build strength
Add balancing poses such as tree or eagle
Come to the floor for seated stretches and forward folds
Include a gentle backbend like cobra or bridge to open the chest
Add hip openers such as pigeon or a seated twist
Breathe into tension and ease off slowly, never bouncing or forcing
Rest in savasana for at least 5 minutes to absorb the practice
Close with a moment of stillness and a slow return to your day

templates.name: Home Workout Checklist
templates.description: Stay fit without a gym — warm up, bodyweight strength, cardio intervals, core, and a proper cool-down.
items: Clear a space about the size of your mat, with room to reach out
Keep water and a towel nearby, and a mat or soft surface for floor work
Warm up for 5 minutes with marching, arm circles, and hip openers
Do a bodyweight strength circuit: squats, push-ups, lunges, and glute bridges
Rest 30 to 60 seconds between rounds, and repeat the circuit 2 to 4 times
Add cardio intervals: jumping jacks, high knees, or burpees
Add load with resistance bands or filled water bottles if you have them
Do focused core work: planks, dead bugs, and bicycle crunches
Keep good form over speed, and stop any move that causes sharp pain
Stay hydrated with small sips throughout
Cool down with 3 to 5 minutes of easy movement to lower your heart rate
Stretch the major muscle groups you worked while they're still warm
Track your exercises, rounds, and reps
Note how it felt so you can adjust the next session

templates.name: New Employee Onboarding Checklist
templates.description: From before day one to the 30-day review — accounts, paperwork, goals, and check-ins, in order.
items: Before day 1: confirm the signed offer, contract, and start details
Before day 1: set up their email, accounts, and hardware — laptop, badge, and logins
Before day 1: prepare their desk, or ship equipment ahead for a remote start
Before day 1: assign a buddy or mentor and share a first-week schedule
Day 1: welcome them, give an office or virtual tour, and introduce the team
Day 1: complete HR paperwork, tax forms, and payroll setup
Day 1: review the role, expectations, and 30/60/90-day goals
Day 1: grant system access and walk through the key tools they'll use
Week 1: set up recurring 1:1s with their manager and key teammates
Week 1: share team docs, processes, and communication norms
Week 1: assign a small, achievable first task to build early momentum
Week 1: complete required training and any compliance or security modules
Week 1: add them to relevant meetings, channels, and mailing lists
First month: check in regularly and ask for their early feedback
First month: review the 30-day goals together and adjust
First month: introduce them to cross-functional partners they'll work with
First month: confirm benefits enrollment is complete
First month: run a 30-day onboarding review to see how they're settling in

templates.name: Project Kickoff Checklist
templates.description: Set a project up to succeed — goals, scope, roles, timeline, risks, and a clean kickoff meeting.
items: Define the project goal, scope, and success criteria
Identify the stakeholders and, crucially, the single decision-maker
Confirm the budget and the resources you actually have
Assemble the team and confirm each person's availability
Define roles and responsibilities so ownership is unambiguous
Gather and document the requirements
Break the work into milestones and a realistic timeline
Identify dependencies and risks, and note a mitigation for each
Choose your tools for tracking, docs, and communication
Set up the project workspace: the board, repo, or shared folder
Agree on a communication cadence and how status gets reported
Define what done looks like for the first milestone
Schedule the kickoff meeting and send an agenda in advance
Run the kickoff: align on goals, plan, roles, and next steps
Document the decisions made and share the notes with everyone
Confirm the first tasks and their owners before you close the kickoff

templates.name: Meeting Prep Checklist
templates.description: Run tighter meetings — a real purpose, an agenda, the right people, and clear next steps.
items: Define the meeting's purpose and the outcome you want
Decide whether a meeting is actually needed, or if an email or doc would do
Invite only the people who genuinely need to be there
Write an agenda and share it ahead of time
Set a clear start and end time, and keep it as short as it can be
Assign a facilitator to run it and a note-taker to capture decisions
Send any pre-reads or materials in advance
Book the room or set up and share the video link
Test the AV, screen sharing, and any demo beforehand
Prepare your slides, data, or demo
List the specific decisions that must be made in the meeting
Come with a proposed recommendation, not just open questions
Plan time for discussion and for agreeing next steps
Keep a parking lot for off-topic items so they don't derail the agenda
Know who owns following up on the action items afterward

templates.name: Remote Work Setup Checklist
templates.description: Set up a productive home office — internet, ergonomics, gear, security, and healthy boundaries.
items: Reliable high-speed internet, plus a backup like a phone hotspot
A dedicated desk or workspace, separate from where you relax
An ergonomic, adjustable chair that supports your back
An external monitor at eye level to keep your neck neutral
An external keyboard and mouse
Good lighting: natural light plus a task lamp
A quality webcam and a headset with a mic for clear calls
A reliable laptop or computer that meets your job's requirements
VPN and security tools installed and configured
Access to all work accounts and tools, ideally via SSO and a password manager
Communication apps set up: chat, video, and email
Cloud storage and file access configured
A tidy or virtual background for video calls
Cable management and a surge-protected power strip
Set working hours and share your availability and status
A shutdown routine to end the workday and protect your time off
Know who to contact for IT support
A water bottle and a plan for regular breaks

templates.name: Daily Standup Checklist
templates.description: Keep the daily standup short and useful — the three questions, blockers, and clear next steps.
items: Keep it to 15 minutes, timeboxed
Same time, same place (or link), every working day
Everyone stands or stays on camera to keep it brief
Each person shares what they did yesterday
Each person shares what they're doing today
Each person names any blockers
Update the board or tracker before or during standup so it reflects reality
Flag blockers clearly and name who can help unblock them
Take detailed discussions offline: "let's take that after standup"
Note action items and their owners
Keep the focus on progress toward the sprint or team goal
Don't let it become a status report aimed at the manager
Rotate or assign a facilitator to keep time and flow
Follow up on yesterday's blockers to make sure they got resolved
End with clear next steps and who's doing what

templates.name: Job Interview Checklist
templates.description: Research, STAR answers, questions to ask, logistics, and a strong follow-up.
items: Research the company: what it sells, recent news, and its mission
Re-read the job description and match your experience to each requirement
Prepare stories for common questions using the STAR method
Prepare three to five thoughtful questions to ask the interviewer
Look up your interviewers on LinkedIn if you know their names
Practice a clear, confident introduction out loud
Choose and lay out your outfit the night before
Print several copies of your resume and a list of references
Bring a notepad, pen, and any portfolio or work samples that fit the role
Confirm the date, time, format, and location or video link
Plan your route to arrive ten to fifteen minutes early
Prepare a salary range you'd accept, in case it comes up
Silence your phone and bring a bottle of water
Have questions ready about next steps and the timeline
Send a short, specific thank-you email within 24 hours
Write down notes right after, while the details are fresh

templates.name: First Day at Work Checklist
templates.description: What to bring, arriving early, setup, meeting the team, and first-week priorities.
items: Confirm your start time, location or video link, and who to ask for
Bring your ID and any documents HR requested
Lay out a professional outfit that matches the team's dress code
Plan your commute to arrive ten to fifteen minutes early
Pack lunch or know your options nearby, plus a water bottle
Bring a notebook and pen to capture names, systems, and to-dos
Learn the names of your manager and immediate teammates
Set up your workstation, email, accounts, and required software
Read the onboarding materials, handbook, and key policies
Ask about the logins and access you'll need for your role
Note your key contacts: IT, HR, your manager, and a go-to teammate
Ask your manager what your first-week priorities are
Write questions down as they come up instead of interrupting constantly
Learn the basics: where things are, how to book rooms, how expenses work
Say yes to lunch or coffee to start building relationships
Review your notes at the end of the day and confirm tomorrow's plan

templates.name: Weekly Work Review Checklist
templates.description: Close out the week and plan the next — review, inbox, priorities, and reflection.
items: Review what you finished this week against what you planned
Check progress on each ongoing project and flag anything at risk
Capture loose ends: unread messages, half-done tasks, open loops
Clear and organize your inbox to a manageable state
Follow up on anything you're waiting on from other people
Review next week's calendar, deadlines, and meetings
Update your task list and set the top three priorities for next week
Note key decisions and update project docs while they're fresh
Reflect on what went well and what you'd do again
Pick one thing to improve or handle differently next week
Log your wins and progress for later reviews
Check in on your longer-term goals, not just this week's tasks
Tidy your files, desktop, and notes so Monday starts clean
Block focus time for your most important work next week
Note anything to raise with your manager or team

templates.name: Exam Prep Checklist
templates.description: A 2-week timeline to revision — schedule, past papers, active recall, and the night before, in order.
items: Two weeks out: list every topic on the syllabus and mark each as strong, shaky, or not started
Two weeks out: gather your notes, textbook, past papers, and the exam format and mark scheme
Two weeks out: build a revision timetable that gives weak topics more sessions than strong ones
12 days out: start with active recall — close the book and write what you remember, then check
10 days out: turn your weak topics into flashcards or a one-page summary each
9 days out: do your first past paper untimed, with notes, to find the gaps
7 days out: teach a tricky topic out loud to someone, or to an empty room
6 days out: do a full past paper under real exam conditions and time yourself
5 days out: mark your paper against the scheme and re-revise every question you lost marks on
4 days out: space short recall sessions across all topics rather than one long block
3 days out: memorize the formulas, dates, or definitions you still can't recall cold
2 days out: do a final timed paper, then review only your weakest two topics
Day before: pack your bag — ID, pens, calculator, water, and any permitted notes
Day before: confirm the exam time, room, and route, and set two alarms
Day before: stop revising by early evening, eat well, and get a full night's sleep
Exam morning: eat breakfast, skim your one-page summaries, and arrive early

templates.name: College Packing Checklist
templates.description: Dorm move-in essentials — bedding, storage, study gear, kitchen basics, and documents.
items: Twin XL sheets, a mattress topper, pillows, and a comforter
Mattress protector and an extra set of sheets
Bath towels, a hand towel, and a quick-dry shower towel
Shower caddy and flip-flops for shared bathrooms
Toiletries, a toothbrush holder, and a refillable water bottle
Laptop, charger, and a padded sleeve or bag
Power strip with surge protection and a couple of extension cords
Phone charger, headphones, and any adapters you need
Desk lamp and a small clip-on reading light
Notebooks, pens, highlighters, sticky notes, and a planner
Backpack for class and a reusable water bottle
Under-bed storage bins and a few drawer organizers
Laundry hamper, detergent pods, and a roll of quarters or a laundry card
Basic first-aid kit and any daily medications
Mini fridge or microwave — coordinate so you and your roommate don't both bring one
A few mugs, plates, utensils, and a reusable food container
Command hooks, poster strips, and a small toolkit
Fan, plus a warm blanket or throw for cold nights
Important documents: ID, insurance card, and a copy of your housing and class schedule
A little decor — photos, string lights, or a rug to make the room yours

templates.name: Back to School Supplies Checklist
templates.description: The school-supply basics — notebooks, writing tools, backpack, organizers, and a first-day kit.
items: Backpack that fits a laptop or binders comfortably
Spiral notebooks, or a binder with loose-leaf paper, for each subject
Pens in black and blue, pencils, and a good eraser
Highlighters in a few colors and a set of markers
Pencil case or pouch to keep it all in one place
Ruler, scissors, and a glue stick
Sticky notes, index cards, and paper clips
Folders or dividers to sort handouts by subject
A planner or academic calendar for deadlines
Scientific or graphing calculator, if your math class needs one
Laptop or tablet and its charger
Headphones for library work and online lessons
USB drive or a cloud storage account for backups
Water bottle and a reusable lunch bag or box
Hand sanitizer and a small pack of tissues
Sticky tabs and a stapler for organizing notes
Whiteboard markers or a small dry-erase board for revision
A reusable tote for gym kit or extra books
A first-day kit: schedule, locker combo, ID, and a bit of cash

templates.name: Thesis Writing Checklist
templates.description: A step-by-step path from topic and proposal through drafting, editing, and submission, in order.
items: Choose and narrow your topic into a specific, answerable research question
Confirm your supervisor and agree on scope, expectations, and a rough timeline
Do a literature review and map what has already been written on your question
Write and get approval for your proposal or research plan
Choose your methodology and, if needed, get ethics or data approval
Set up a reference manager and log every source as you read
Build a chapter outline with a target word count for each section
Collect and analyze your data or primary material
Draft the body chapters first — methods, results, and discussion
Write the introduction and literature review to frame the finished body
Write the conclusion, tying findings back to your original question
Write the abstract last, summarizing the whole thesis in one page
Revise for argument and structure — does each chapter earn its place?
Proofread for grammar, and check every citation and reference for accuracy
Format to your department's guidelines: title page, contents, margins, and numbering
Run a final plagiarism check and submit before the deadline, keeping a backup copy

templates.name: Study Plan Checklist
templates.description: Build a realistic study schedule step by step — goals, topics, time blocks, and progress tracking.
items: Set a specific, measurable goal and its deadline
List every topic or chapter you need to cover
Rate each topic by how well you know it and how heavily it is weighted
Estimate how many study sessions each topic needs
Look at your real week and find the hours you can protect for study
Block those hours in a calendar as fixed appointments
Break study into focused blocks with short breaks, like 25 or 50 minutes on, then a rest
Front-load weak topics early, while your energy and runway are highest
Build in spaced repetition — revisit each topic several times, not once
Choose an active method for each session: recall, past questions, or teaching it aloud
Add buffer days for catch-up and the topics that run long
Track what you finish and check off each session as you go
Review the plan weekly and shift time toward whatever is still shaky
Protect sleep, meals, and one rest day so you don't burn out
Do a final review pass over everything a few days before the deadline

templates.name: Online Course Checklist
templates.description: Set up your space, map deadlines, keep up with lectures, and track progress to the finish.
items: Set up a dedicated, distraction-free space and confirm your internet, sound, and logins work
Read the full syllabus and note the grading breakdown and what's due when
Add every deadline — assignments, quizzes, exams — to your calendar at the start
Block a regular weekly slot for the course so it doesn't quietly slip
Watch each lecture actively, pausing to take notes in your own words
Keep up with assigned readings before the related lecture, not after
Summarize the key ideas after each module while they're fresh
Take part in discussion forums or live sessions
Start assignments early enough to ask questions before they're due
Review your notes regularly instead of cramming before quizzes
Reach out to the instructor or classmates when you're stuck, rather than stalling
Track which modules you've finished against the total
Back up your notes and submitted work somewhere safe
Apply what you learn in a small project or practice problem
Save your certificate and course materials when you finish

templates.name: Research Paper Checklist
templates.description: A step-by-step path from topic and sources through drafting, citing, editing, and submitting on time.
items: Read the assignment closely: length, format, citation style, and due date
Choose a topic that genuinely interests you and narrow it to a focused question
Do background reading to see what exists and where you can add something
Gather credible sources, saving full citation details for each as you go
Develop a clear, arguable thesis statement
Build an outline that maps your argument section by section
Write a first draft without stopping to perfect every sentence
Support each point with evidence and cite every source you use
Write the introduction and conclusion once the body is in place
Check that each paragraph makes one clear point that serves the thesis
Format in-text citations and the bibliography in the required style
Revise for structure and argument first, then edit for grammar and clarity
Run a plagiarism check and confirm every source is properly credited
Proofread a final time — after a break, or by reading it aloud
Submit before the deadline and keep a backup copy
