templates.name: Deep Cleaning Checklist
templates.description: The twice-a-year deep clean — skirting boards, appliance filters, limescale, and the spots a weekly tidy skips.
items: Dust from the top down: light fixtures, ceiling corners, and the tops of doorframes and wardrobes
Wash walls, switch plates, and skirting boards with a damp microfiber cloth
Clean windows inside and out, including the tracks and sills
Launder the curtains and wipe down blinds slat by slat
Descale the kettle and coffee machine with a vinegar or citric-acid solution
Degrease the extractor hood and soak or replace its filter
Deep-clean the oven: remove the racks to soak, and scrub the interior glass
Pull out the fridge, defrost the freezer, and wipe the coils and door seals
Empty and wipe every kitchen cupboard, checking food dates while you're in there
Run an empty hot cycle with cleaner in the washing machine and dishwasher
Scrub the grout and re-caulk any mouldy sealant around the bath and sink
Descale the showerhead by soaking it in vinegar overnight
Disinfect and descale the toilet, including the base and behind the bowl
Vacuum and flip the mattresses, and wash mattress protectors and pillows
Wash or dry-clean duvets, and vacuum the divan or bed base
Move furniture to vacuum underneath, then shampoo carpets or mop hard floors
Wipe down radiators and vacuum the dust from between the fins
Disinfect high-touch spots: light switches, door handles, and remote controls
Vacuum upholstered sofas and chairs, including under the cushions
Empty, wash, and disinfect every bin, including the kitchen caddy

templates.name: Move Out Cleaning Checklist
templates.description: The end-of-tenancy clean that gets your deposit back — in the order landlords inspect.
items: Start once the place is empty: open the windows, and gather bin bags, cloths, and cleaners before you begin
Kitchen first: empty every cupboard and drawer, then wipe them inside and out
Deep-clean the oven, hob, grill, and extractor filter
Defrost, empty, and wipe the fridge and freezer, and leave the doors ajar if you're switching them off
Descale the kettle, and clean the sink, taps, and any tiled splashback
Bathroom next: descale the toilet, taps, and showerhead, and scrub limescale off the screen
Clean and re-whiten the grout, and wipe mould off the silicone sealant
Polish the mirrors, chrome, and glass until they're streak-free
Wipe down all interior doors, handles, and light switches
Clean the inside and outside of every window, plus the sills and tracks
Dust and wipe skirting boards, radiators, and picture rails throughout
Remove cobwebs from ceiling corners and light fittings in every room
Fill nail holes and wipe scuffs off the walls
Wipe inside all built-in wardrobes and storage cupboards
Clean any supplied appliances — the washing machine drawer, dishwasher filter, and microwave
Take a full set of dated photos once each room is done, as proof of its condition
Vacuum every room, including inside the cupboards and along the edges
Mop the hard floors and shampoo or spot-clean the carpets, working toward the front door last

templates.name: Spring Cleaning Checklist
templates.description: The once-a-year refresh — declutter, wash away winter, and reset every room.
items: Open every window to air out the whole home before you start
Declutter room by room, sorting into keep, donate, sell, and bin piles
Wash the windows inside and out, and clean the tracks, sills, and screens
Launder or dry-clean the curtains, and dust the blinds slat by slat
Take down and wash light fittings and lampshades, and replace any dead bulbs
Dust ceiling corners, cornices, and the tops of doorframes and wardrobes
Wipe walls, skirting boards, switch plates, and door handles
Vacuum and flip the mattresses, and wash duvets, pillows, and protectors
Swap the wardrobe over to the new season, and donate what didn't get worn
Empty, wipe, and reorganize kitchen cupboards, checking food dates as you go
Deep-clean the oven, and degrease the extractor hood and its filter
Defrost the freezer, and wipe the fridge shelves and door seals
Descale the kettle, coffee machine, and showerhead
Scrub the bathroom grout and refresh any discoloured sealant
Wipe down radiators and clear the dust from between the fins
Clean behind and underneath the heavy furniture and appliances
Shampoo carpets and rugs, and mop and polish the hard floors
Wipe the front and inside of every kitchen appliance and small gadget
Clean and disinfect the bins, and replace worn cloths and sponges
Tackle one outdoor job: sweep the patio, wash the doormat, or clean the bins

templates.name: Daily Cleaning Checklist
templates.description: The 15-minute daily reset that stops mess piling up — dishes, surfaces, and a quick tidy.
items: Make the beds as soon as everyone is up
Wash the dishes, or load and run the dishwasher, after each meal
Wipe down the kitchen counters and the hob after cooking
Clear and wipe the dining table once the plates are gone
Do a 10-minute tidy: put stray items back where they belong, room by room
Wipe the bathroom sink and taps, and squeegee the shower after use
Run, hang, or fold one load of laundry to stop it piling up
Sweep or spot-vacuum the kitchen floor for crumbs and spills
Take out the kitchen bin if it's full, and reset a fresh liner
Wipe down high-touch spots: door handles, light switches, and taps
Sort the day's post and paperwork so it doesn't pile up
Empty pockets, and put shoes, coats, and bags away by the door
Give the toilet a quick brush and wipe the seat
Fluff the sofa cushions and fold any blankets before bed
Set out what you need for the morning, and give the sink a final wipe

templates.name: House Chores Checklist
templates.description: Every recurring home job — daily, weekly, and monthly — in one shareable list.
items: Daily: wash up or run the dishwasher after meals
Daily: wipe the kitchen counters and the hob
Daily: make the beds and do a quick tidy of each room
Daily: take out the kitchen bin when full and reset the liner
Weekly: change and wash the bed sheets and pillowcases
Weekly: vacuum all carpets and rugs, and mop the hard floors
Weekly: clean the bathroom — toilet, sink, bath, shower, and mirror
Weekly: dust the surfaces, shelves, and electronics throughout
Weekly: wipe the kitchen appliance fronts, the microwave, and the sink
Weekly: do the full laundry, including towels and tea towels
Weekly: empty and wipe out all the household bins
Weekly: water the houseplants and clear away any dead leaves
Monthly: wipe down skirting boards, door handles, and light switches
Monthly: clean the oven and degrease the extractor hood
Monthly: descale the kettle, coffee machine, and showerhead
Monthly: wash the bins, doormats, and any pet bedding
Monthly: run a hot maintenance cycle in the washing machine and dishwasher
Monthly: clean the windows and wipe the sills
Monthly: vacuum under the furniture and behind large appliances
Monthly: check and restock cleaning supplies, and replace worn sponges and cloths

templates.name: Home Maintenance Checklist
templates.description: Seasonal upkeep that prevents costly repairs — roof, gutters, HVAC, detectors, plumbing, and safety checks.
items: Inspect the roof for damaged, loose, or missing shingles or tiles
Clear leaves and debris from gutters and downspouts, and check they drain
Test every smoke and carbon-monoxide detector, and replace the batteries
Change or clean HVAC and furnace filters
Service the heating system before winter and the AC before summer
Check under sinks, around the water heater, and at visible pipes for leaks
Flush the water heater to clear sediment, and test its pressure-relief valve
Clean the dryer's lint trap and exhaust ducting
Test and reset GFCI outlets, and check the breaker panel for issues
Inspect and reseal weather stripping and caulking around doors and windows
Check exterior caulking and grout, and touch up peeling paint or siding
Clean the refrigerator coils so it runs efficiently
Test the garage door's auto-reverse safety feature
Service seasonal equipment: the lawn mower in spring, the snow blower before winter
Trim trees and shrubs back from the roof, siding, and power lines
Check the attic and basement for moisture, pests, or failing insulation
Test the sump pump before the wet season, and clear the pit

templates.name: Product Launch Checklist
templates.description: A step-by-step launch plan — positioning, beta, pricing, launch day, and the follow-up.
items: Nail your positioning: who it's for, the problem it solves, and why it's different
Define the launch goal and the metrics you'll judge it by (signups, revenue, installs)
Set the launch date and work backward into a dated pre-launch timeline
Run a private beta and collect feedback, testimonials, and bug reports
Fix the launch-blocking issues from beta and confirm the release candidate
Finalize pricing, packaging, and any launch-day offer or trial
Write the core messaging and prepare the landing or product page
Prepare launch assets: demo video, screenshots, press kit, and FAQ
Line up distribution: email list, social posts, communities, and any press or creators
Set up analytics, event tracking, and dashboards to measure the launch
Brief support and sales, and prepare canned answers to the likely questions
Do a full dry run: test signup, checkout, onboarding, and the support path end to end
Schedule the launch-day posts, emails, and any submission (directory, marketplace, or press embargo)
Launch: publish the page, send the announcement, and post across your channels
Monitor systems, error rates, and payments closely for the first hours
Engage in real time: reply to comments, questions, and reviews as they come in
Track results against your launch metrics and note what converted best
Follow up with leads, trials, and press who engaged but didn't convert
Gather feedback from new users and triage the first round of fixes
Run a launch retrospective: what worked, what didn't, and what to repeat next time

templates.name: Website Launch Checklist
templates.description: Everything to check before and after go-live — content, SEO, analytics, speed, and security.
items: Proofread every page for typos, broken sentences, and leftover placeholder text
Test every link, button, and navigation menu for dead ends
Check the site on real phones, tablets, and desktop, and across the major browsers
Confirm all images have alt text and are compressed for fast loading
Set up and test every form, and confirm submissions arrive where they should
Add page titles, meta descriptions, and Open Graph tags to each page
Create and submit an XML sitemap and a robots.txt file
Set canonical URLs and resolve any duplicate-content issues
Install analytics and confirm events and conversions actually fire
Run a performance audit and fix slow-loading pages and oversized assets
Confirm HTTPS is enforced and the SSL certificate is valid
Set up 301 redirects from every old URL to its new equivalent
Add a custom 404 page and test that it works
Check accessibility: colour contrast, keyboard navigation, and heading structure
Back up the site and confirm you can actually restore it
Configure security: firewall, spam protection, and two-factor auth on admin
Point the domain and DNS, and confirm the site resolves on www and non-www
Go live, then immediately test the homepage, the checkout or contact path, and the forms
Submit the site to search engines and request indexing of the key pages
Monitor analytics, error logs, and uptime for the first days, and fix what breaks

templates.name: Social Media Content Checklist
templates.description: Run this before every post — hook, value, visuals, tags, and a final proofread.
items: Tie the post to a goal: awareness, engagement, traffic, or conversion
Lead with a strong hook in the first line or frame
Deliver one clear idea or piece of value per post
Match the format to the platform (aspect ratio, length, and style)
Write in the platform's native voice, not one caption copied across all of them
Add a clear call to action — comment, save, share, or click
Include high-quality visuals or video sized correctly for the platform
Add captions or subtitles to any video
Add descriptive alt text to images for accessibility and reach
Use a focused set of relevant hashtags, not a generic wall of them
Check that any link works and is tracked with a UTM or short link
Tag relevant people, brands, or locations where it adds value
Proofread for spelling, grammar, and factual accuracy
Confirm you have the rights to any image, music, or clip you've used
Schedule the post for when your audience is actually active
Cross-post or adapt the content for other channels where it fits
Plan to reply to comments and DMs within the first hour or two
Log the post so you can review what performed and repeat what worked

templates.name: Startup Checklist
templates.description: From idea to first customers — validation, legal, finances, MVP, and launch, in order.
items: Write down the problem you're solving and who has it most painfully
Talk to 20-30 potential customers before building anything
Research the market size, the competitors, and how people solve this today
Define your unique value: why you, why now, and why different
Test demand with a landing page, waitlist, or pre-sale before you build
Sketch a business model: how you make money and what it costs to deliver
Choose a business structure and register the company
Sort the legal basics: licenses, contracts, terms, and a privacy policy
Open a business bank account and set up bookkeeping
Secure the name: domain, a trademark check, and social handles
Build a minimum viable product — the smallest thing that solves the core problem
Set up basic branding: a logo, colours, and a simple one-page website
Get a few pilot users onto the MVP and gather honest feedback
Iterate on the product until users see clear, repeatable value
Set pricing based on value and what the market will bear
Set up payments, invoicing, and the tools to fulfill or deliver
Plan how you'll reach customers: the one or two channels you'll focus on
Launch to your waitlist and first target audience
Land your first paying customers and learn from every objection
Track your key numbers and decide what to double down on or change

templates.name: Small Business Setup Checklist
templates.description: Everything to set up a small business — plan, register, finances, tax, and licenses.
items: Write a simple business plan: what you sell, to whom, and how you'll make money
Choose a business structure (sole trader, LLC, partnership, or company)
Pick and check your business name for availability and trademark conflicts
Register the business with the relevant government authority
Register for tax and get any required tax ID or number
Check which licenses or permits your trade and location require
Open a dedicated business bank account
Set up bookkeeping or accounting software from day one
Get the business insurance your trade needs (liability, professional, contents)
Set up a system to track income, expenses, and receipts for tax time
Choose how you'll take payment: card reader, online checkout, or invoicing
Set your prices and payment terms, and prepare an invoice template
Register a domain and set up a professional email address
Build a simple website or listing so customers can find and contact you
Set up the tools you'll run the business on (calendar, storage, comms)
Sort out suppliers, stock, or the equipment you need to deliver
Understand your record-keeping and tax-filing deadlines
Do a soft launch to test your systems before you open fully

templates.name: Apartment Viewing Checklist
templates.description: What to check before you sign — water pressure, damp, heating, noise, appliances, and hidden costs.
items: Turn on the kitchen and bathroom taps to check water pressure and how long hot water takes to arrive
Flip every light switch and plug a charger into each outlet you can reach
Look for water stains, bubbling paint, or a musty smell around ceilings, windows, and under sinks
Open, close, and lock every window, and feel for drafts around the frames
Test the heating and any air conditioning, even if it's the wrong season
Walk the floors for soft spots, loud squeaks, and damage hidden under rugs
Open every closet, cabinet, and storage space and picture where your things will go
Confirm each included appliance actually runs — fridge, oven, stove, dishwasher, washer, dryer
Stand still for a minute and listen for traffic, neighbours, and plumbing noise
Check the mobile signal in each room, including the bedrooms and bathroom
Look under the kitchen sink and around bins for droppings, traps, or roach signs
Check the front-door lock, buzzer or intercom, and how secure the building entrance feels
Ask exactly what the rent includes — water, heating, electricity, internet, parking
Note which way the windows face and how much natural light each room gets
Take photos or a short video of the whole place as you walk through

templates.name: House Inspection Checklist
templates.description: Check roof, foundation, plumbing, wiring, HVAC, damp, and pests before you buy or renew.
items: Check the roof for missing, curling, or patched shingles and note its rough age
Check the gutters and downspouts for sagging, leaks, and where they drain
Walk the foundation and exterior walls, looking for cracks, bulging, or crumbling
Run the taps, showers, and flush the toilets in every bathroom, watching pressure and drainage
Open the electrical panel and check for labelled breakers, scorch marks, and enough capacity
Test the heating and cooling, and ask when the HVAC was last serviced and the filter changed
Look for pest signs — droppings, gnaw marks, mud tubes, sawdust — in the attic, basement, and corners
Check the attic insulation depth and look for daylight, stains, or mould under the roof
Inspect the basement or crawl space for damp, efflorescence, and a musty smell
Open and close the garage door and test its auto-reverse safety
Check that windows and doors open, close, and lock, and look for fogging between double-glazed panes
Look under sinks and around the water heater for leaks, corrosion, and its age
Test a sample of outlets and switches, plus the GFCI outlets in kitchens and bathrooms
Walk the boundaries and compare fences and structures against the property lines
Check for even floors and doors that latch; a door that won't close can signal settling
Hire a licensed inspector for anything structural, electrical, or you can't safely reach

templates.name: Rental Agreement Checklist
templates.description: What to check in a lease before signing — deposit, dates, utilities, repairs, and the fine print.
items: Read the whole lease, including the small print and any addendums, before signing anything
Confirm the rent amount, due date, accepted payment methods, and any late fees
Check the deposit amount, what it covers, and the exact conditions for getting it back
Confirm the lease start and end dates, and whether it renews automatically or goes month-to-month
Read the early-termination clause and what breaking the lease actually costs
Check who pays which utilities and services — water, heat, electricity, gas, internet, trash
Review the pet policy, any pet deposit or rent, and the rules on guests and subletting
Note exactly which repairs and maintenance are yours versus the landlord's
Confirm parking, storage, and any shared-space details in writing
Check the rules on rent increases and how much notice you'll get
Understand the landlord's right of entry and how much notice they must give before visiting
Photograph and video every room before move-in, including existing damage, and share it with the landlord
Make sure every blank in the lease is filled in, and both parties sign and date it
Save the landlord or property manager's name, phone, email, and address for notices
Keep a signed copy of the lease and every receipt and message in one place

templates.name: Home Buying Checklist
templates.description: Step by step from budget and pre-approval to inspection, insurance, closing costs, and keys.
items: Check your credit and pay down what you can before applying
Set a realistic budget that includes the down payment and monthly costs, not just the price
Get a mortgage pre-approval so you know your true price range and can move fast
Research neighbourhoods, commute, schools, and how the area feels at different times
Make a must-have versus nice-to-have list to keep viewings focused
Line up and attend viewings, and compare each place against your list
Make an offer and negotiate the price and terms with your agent
Hire a licensed home inspector once your offer is accepted
Review the property title, survey, and history for liens, disputes, or easements
Get the property appraised, which your lender will usually require
Compare home insurance quotes and lock in a policy before closing
Budget for closing costs on top of the down payment
Do a final walk-through to confirm the condition and that agreed repairs are done
Review and sign the closing documents, and keep copies of everything
Set up utilities, change your address, and collect the keys and any codes or manuals

templates.name: Seasonal Wardrobe Checklist
templates.description: Refresh your closet smartly — clear out, spot real gaps, pick a palette, and buy versatile basics.
items: Take everything out and sort it into keep, repair, and let go
Try on the keep pile and check fit, wear, and whether you actually reach for it
Note the real gaps: what you own but can't complete an outfit with
Pick a small colour palette so new pieces mix with what you already own
List the basics worth replacing — worn-out staples do more work than trend pieces
Set a budget and decide where it's worth spending more versus saving
Check the weather you actually dress for, not just the calendar season
Read care labels before buying — dry-clean-only adds hidden cost and effort
Feel the fabric and check the seams, buttons, and stitching for quality
Favour versatile pieces that work across several outfits and occasions
Try things on rather than guessing your size across brands
Compare prices across stores and check for end-of-season sales before buying
Keep receipts and tags until you're sure, and note the return windows
Donate, sell, or recycle what you're letting go rather than letting it pile up
Store off-season clothes clean and protected to make room and keep them fresh

templates.name: Electronics Buying Checklist
templates.description: Make smart tech buys — match your needs, compare models and prices, check reviews and warranty.
items: Write down what you actually need the device to do before you shop
Set a budget range, and decide whether last year's model at a discount does the job
Shortlist a few models and compare the specs that actually matter for your use
Read recent user reviews, not just the star rating, for real-world problems
Search the model name plus 'problems' or 'recall' to check for common faults
Confirm it's compatible with what you already own — cables, ports, ecosystem, software
Compare prices across several retailers, including refurbished and open-box
Check whether a sale is coming up before you buy at full price
Read the return policy and return window before buying, especially online
Check the warranty length and what it actually covers
See which accessories are included and which you'll need to buy separately
Factor in running costs — subscriptions, batteries, ink, storage, or energy use
Buy from a reputable seller to avoid counterfeits and warranty problems
Keep the receipt, warranty, and box until you're sure it works and you're keeping it
Register the product and install any updates or security before daily use

templates.name: Gift Shopping Checklist
templates.description: Find the right gifts without the stress — budget, ideas, tracking, early ordering, and receipts.
items: List everyone you're buying for so no one gets forgotten at the last minute
Set a total budget and a rough amount per person
Jot down each person's interests, hobbies, sizes, and anything they've hinted at
Check for wish lists or registries before guessing
Note sizes and any allergies or preferences for clothing, food, or beauty gifts
Brainstorm a few ideas per person across a range of prices
Consider experiences or consumables for people who already have plenty of stuff
Consider a handmade or personalised gift where it fits — they carry more meaning
Track what you've bought, for whom, and where, in one running list
Order early to beat shipping deadlines and stock running out
Check delivery dates and any customs or shipping fees for gifts sent abroad
Buy wrapping paper, gift bags, tape, and cards in one trip
Ask for gift receipts and keep them somewhere you'll find them
Set aside time to wrap rather than leaving it all to the last night
Keep a couple of small spare gifts on hand for anyone you missed

templates.name: Doctor Visit Checklist
templates.description: What to bring, symptoms to note, and questions to ask so you make the most of your appointment.
items: Write down your main reason for the visit and what you hope to resolve
List your current symptoms — when each started, how often, and what makes it better or worse
Bring an up-to-date list of your medications and doses, including supplements
Note any allergies and past reactions to medications
Write your questions in priority order
Pack your insurance card and a photo ID
Gather recent test results, scans, or reports from other clinics
Note relevant family medical history, such as heart disease, diabetes, or cancer
Bring home-tracked numbers if you monitor them — blood pressure, blood sugar, or weight
List other doctors or specialists you see, and what they treat
Confirm the date, time, location, and any prep like fasting or forms
Have a way to take notes during the visit — a small notepad or your phone
Arrange for someone to come along if you'd like a second set of ears
Know which pharmacy you use so any new prescription can be sent there

templates.name: Medication Tracker Checklist
templates.description: Track doses, refill dates, and side effects, and keep an up-to-date list ready for every appointment.
items: List every medication you take, with its brand and generic name
Record the dose and exactly when you take each one
Note what each medication is for
Set daily reminders for each dose time
Track refill dates and reorder a few days early
Write down any side effects and when they started, to share with your doctor
Ask your pharmacist to check for interactions whenever a new medication is added
Keep your pharmacy's name, phone number, and hours saved
Store medications as directed — cool, dry, and out of reach of children
Note any special instructions, like taking with food or avoiding certain drinks
Keep a copy of the list in your wallet or phone for emergencies
Bring the current list to every appointment and update it after changes
Safely dispose of expired or discontinued medications
Review the whole list with your doctor at least once a year

templates.name: Dental Visit Checklist
templates.description: What to bring, concerns to raise, and questions to ask so your dental appointment goes smoothly.
items: Confirm the date, time, and location, and add it to your calendar
Bring your insurance or dental plan card and a photo ID
Brush and floss before you go
Write down any concerns — a sensitive tooth, bleeding gums, jaw pain, or a chip
List your current medications and any recent changes
Update your medical history form, including allergies
Prepare questions about brushing, flossing, whitening, or a treatment you're weighing
Arrange a ride ahead of time if you're having sedation or a procedure
Bring any prior X-rays or records if you're seeing a new dentist
Arrive about 15 minutes early to fill out forms
Ask about anything flagged during the exam and what your options are
Confirm the cost and what your insurance covers before agreeing to treatment
Book your next cleaning before you leave
Schedule any follow-up treatment and note the aftercare instructions

templates.name: Dinner Party Menu Checklist
templates.description: Plan the courses, drinks, shopping, and timeline so dinner comes together calmly and on time.
items: Confirm your guest count and check for allergies or dietary needs
Pick a loose theme or cuisine to tie the courses together
Plan an appetizer or two that can be served cold or at room temperature
Choose a main course you're comfortable cooking, plus two sides
Balance the menu so not everything needs the oven or stove at once
Select a dessert you can make the day before
Plan drinks — wine or a signature cocktail, plus a non-alcoholic option
Write a full shopping list grouped by store section, and note what you already have
Shop for non-perishables and drinks a few days ahead; buy fresh items the day before
Prep what you can in advance — chop, marinate, make sauces, and set out serving dishes
Write a cooking timeline that counts backward from serving time
Set the table and arrange serving spoons and platters earlier in the day
Have a simple backup ready in case a dish doesn't work out
Plan seating, music, and a tidy space for coats and bags

templates.name: Baking Day Checklist
templates.description: Gather tools, measure accurately, mind the oven, and cool and store right for bakes that work.
items: Pick your recipes and read each one all the way through before starting
Check you have every ingredient in the right amount, and note any substitutions
Take butter, eggs, and dairy out early if the recipe wants them at room temperature
Gather all tools — bowls, whisk, mixer, pans, parchment, and a scale
Grease and line your pans before you start mixing
Measure ingredients precisely, ideally by weight with a kitchen scale
Preheat the oven and check it with an oven thermometer
Follow the mixing method exactly — creaming, folding, and order all matter
Set a timer for each batch and check a few minutes before it's due
Test for doneness with a skewer, a gentle press, or the internal temperature
Cool bakes on a wire rack so the bottoms don't turn soggy
Decorate, glaze, or dust once everything has cooled
Store each item the right way once cool
Clean as you go and wash tools between mixing wet and dry ingredients

templates.name: Kitchen Essentials Checklist
templates.description: Pantry staples, oils and spices, fresh basics, and the tools worth keeping in a working kitchen.
items: Stock cooking fats — a neutral oil, olive oil, and butter
Keep vinegars and acids on hand, like white, balsamic, and a lemon or two
Restock everyday spices and dried herbs, and toss any that have lost their smell
Keep baking basics — flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt
Stock pantry carbs like rice, pasta, and a few tins of beans or lentils
Keep flavor builders — garlic, onions, stock cubes, soy sauce, and tomato paste
Restock dairy and eggs, plus a long-life milk or alternative as backup
Buy fresh fruits and vegetables you'll actually use this week
Check expiration and best-before dates and rotate older items to the front
Restock kitchen paper, foil, parchment, cling film, and storage bags
Check dish soap, sponges, and surface cleaner
Replace worn-out tools — a dull knife, a scratched pan, or a cracked spatula
Make sure you have the basics — a chef's knife, cutting board, and a few good pans
Organize shelves and containers so you can see what you have

templates.name: Monthly Budget Checklist
templates.description: Review spending, compare it to your plan, cut unused subscriptions, and set a savings goal each month.
items: Gather your bank, card, and cash records for the month
Note your total income for the month
List and categorize every expense — housing, food, transport, and the rest
Compare what you spent against what you planned, category by category
Flag the categories that went over and note why
Review recurring subscriptions and memberships, and cancel what you no longer use
Scan for any fees, unfamiliar charges, or double bills
Check upcoming large or irregular expenses and set money aside now
Note how much you saved this month and compare it to your goal
Set a savings target for the coming month
Review your debt balances and the payments due
Update your budget or tracking spreadsheet with this month's numbers
Confirm or set up an automatic transfer to savings on payday
Review your progress toward longer-term financial goals
Pick one thing to change next month and write it down

templates.name: Tax Preparation Checklist
templates.description: Gather every document you need to file — income, investment, deduction, and health records — in one place.
items: Confirm the filing deadline for your region and put it in your calendar
Gather all income statements from employers and any freelance or contract work
Collect records of interest, dividends, and any investment gains or sales
Pull together receipts and records for deductible expenses
Organize records of charitable donations
Gather mortgage, property tax, and loan interest statements
Collect health insurance and medical expense documents
Assemble records for any home-office or self-employment expenses
Review last year's return to catch anything recurring you might forget
Note any life changes this year — marriage, a new child, a move, a new job — that affect your taxes
List the credits and deductions you may qualify for, to check or discuss
Have your bank details ready for a refund or the account you'll pay from
Decide whether you'll file yourself or with an accountant, and book them early
Set aside money in case you owe a payment
Keep a complete copy of the return and its supporting documents

templates.name: Investment Review Checklist
templates.description: Review performance, asset mix, fees, and contributions against your plan — organized, not advice.
items: Note the date and pull current statements for every investment account
Review performance since your last check, not just the last few days
Compare your current asset mix against your target allocation
Note any holding that has grown well above or fallen well below its target weight
Review the fees and expense ratios you're paying on each holding
Check that dividends and interest are handled the way you want — reinvested or paid out
Review your retirement contributions and whether you're on track for the year
Confirm you've used any tax-advantaged accounts or annual allowances available to you
Revisit your risk tolerance and time horizon — has anything in your life changed?
Check that beneficiary and account details are current
Note whether rebalancing is needed to return to your target mix
Confirm your investments still match your original plan and goals
Write down the reasoning behind any change you decide to make
Set a date for your next review

templates.name: Financial Goals Checklist
templates.description: Plan and track savings targets, emergency fund, debt payoff, insurance, and retirement in one place.
items: List your short-term goals (under a year) with a target amount and date for each
Set medium- and long-term goals — a home, education, retirement — with rough figures
Check your emergency fund against a few months of essential expenses
List every debt with its balance, interest rate, and minimum payment
Note your debt-payoff progress since your last review
Decide a monthly savings amount and where each portion goes
Review your insurance coverage — health, life, home, vehicle — for gaps
Plan and price out any major purchases coming up
Note your retirement target and whether contributions are on track
Check your credit report and score, and flag any errors
Review beneficiaries, a will, or estate documents if you have them
Track your net worth — what you own minus what you owe — to see the trend
Rank your goals so you know what to fund first when money is tight
Schedule your next review — quarterly works well
